story: The hotel I worked at in Kochi, Kerala terminated me on Monday 12 October 2026. They still have not paid my September 2026 salary of Rs 26,500, or anything for the 12 days I worked in October.

rules.name: wage_due_date
rules.message: After your last day (12 Oct 2026), the law says final wages must be paid within two working days - about 14 Oct 2026 (not counting Sundays and national holidays; your State can set a different limit).
rules.label: When final pay was due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 07 Oct 2029 (1064 days left). This counts 3 years from 07 Oct 2026 (when September 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 2 month(s) x Rs 26,500 = Rs 53,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

support.text: You are an employee because you worked for hire or reward.
support.reason: The law text defines 'employee' as a person employed on wages by an establishment to do any work 'for hire or reward', which directly supports the sentence stating that being an employee requires working 'for hire or reward'.

support.text: Your employer must pay your final wages within two working days of your termination on 12 October 2026.
support.reason: The law text in section 17(2) states that where an employee has been 'removed or dismissed from service', the wages payable shall be paid within two working days of his removal or dismissal. The sentence applies this rule to termination on 12 October 2026, which is a permissible application of the legal rule.

The law text defines 'wages' as all remuneration expressed in terms of money or capable of being so expressed, but it does not specify any particular amount such as Rs 53,000. The sentence asserts a specific unpaid wage amount that is not contained in or directly implied by the law text.

The law text in section 45 deals with appointment of authorities to hear and determine claims, compensation, recovery procedures, and time limits for filing applications. It does not define or state anything about what 'unpaid wages' are or what specific amount they might be. The sentence asserts a specific unpaid wage amount of Rs 53,000 that is not in the law text.

support.text: You must file your claim within three years from 7 October 2029.
support.reason: The law text in section 45(6) states that 'The application under sub-section (4) may be filed within a period of three years from the date on which claims referred to in sub-section (1) arises'. The sentence states 'You must file your claim within three years from 7 October 2029'. The law text does not specify 7 October 2029 as the date from which the three-year period runs; rather, the three years run from 'the date on which claims...arises'. The sentence adds a specific date that is not in the law text.

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
